title: Embedding Model Selection & Optimization
description: Choose optimal embedding models, understand quantization tradeoffs, and optimize embedding generation for latency, cost, and accuracy.

data.text: Not all embedding models are created equal. The choice depends on domain specificity, latency requirements, cost constraints, and the downstream task (semantic search, clustering, classification). Understanding dimensional tradeoffs, instruction-following capabilities, and multilingual support is critical for RAG effectiveness.

Quantization reduces model size and inference latency by lowering numerical precision (e.g., FP32 → INT8 or FP4). For embeddings, this introduces a tradeoff: smaller models fit more in GPU/CPU cache and reduce cost, but degraded embedding quality can significantly hurt retrieval accuracy. The key is measuring the accuracy-cost curve empirically for your specific domain.

data.text: Modern embedding models like text-embedding-3-large and E5 are trained with instructions. Prefixing input text with a task-specific instruction (e.g., 'Represent the query for retrieval:') dramatically improves performance on retrieval tasks. This is especially important when your corpus contains diverse content types (prose, tables, code).

data.text: Measure embedding quality with domain-specific datasets. Use Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) rather than generic benchmarks. A 3% accuracy gain from a better model often pays for itself in reduced hallucinations downstream.

Dimension reduction via PCA or SVD after embedding can reduce storage and improve ANN index speed, but may degrade retrieval quality. Always validate that dimensionality reduction doesn't hurt your retrieval metrics before applying it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Choose embedding models based on domain, cost, and latency tradeoffs
text-embedding-3-small is ideal for cost-sensitive, general-purpose RAG
Instruction-following models benefit from task-specific prefixes
Quantize only after measuring acceptable accuracy degradation
Cache embeddings aggressively — identical inputs produce identical vectors
data.takeaway: Embedding optimization is an empirical process. Measure, iterate, and profile with real domain data before and after every change.
